_comment: Equity risk premiums by market. Vendored deliberately rather than fetched:
Damodaran republishes twice a year (January, with a mid-year update in July), so
an xlsx parser on the request path would be fragile for no benefit and would put a
network call inside the offline test suite. Updating this file is a manual, dated
act — which is the point. The figure it replaces was invented; this one is sourced.
STRUCTURE — read before editing. Damodaran's country figure is ADDITIVE:
total_erp = mature_market_erp + country_risk_premium
Only `total_erp` is consumed. `country_risk_premium` and `default_spread` are
carried for audit, NOT to be added to anything — adding a CRP on top of a total
ERP double-counts the country. A test pins this.
Cross-check on retrieval: all three markets imply the same mature-market premium
(4.46-0.23 = 5.01-0.78 = 5.14-0.91 = 4.23), which is what the additive structure
requires. If a future update fails that check, the figures were misread.
KEYED BY REPORTING CURRENCY, not country. `info['country']` is None on all seven
fixtures and is not in the get_fundamentals whitelist, so currency is the only
market signal available — the same approximation TAX_RATE_BY_CURRENCY already
makes, and it fails the same way for an issuer whose trading currency is not its
risk domicile. The currency chosen is `financialCurrency`, the one the discounted
cash flows are actually denominated in, because that is what the discount rate has
to match. 0700.HK reports CNY, so it is priced off China, not Hong Kong.
source: Aswath Damodaran, NYU Stern — Country Default Spreads and Risk Premiums
